title: Day 785: Woman Shot Dead at Her Tortilla Stand in Culiacán's 5 de Febrero Neighborhood
detail: Around 3:30 PM on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, a 52-year-old woman identified as Adela 'N', who lived in the La Cascada neighborhood and made and sold handmade flour and corn tortillas, was shot repeatedly and killed at the small wooden stand she operated on Convención de Apatzingán street in the Ampliación 5 de Febrero neighborhood of southeastern Culiacán. A man approached the stand and opened fire before fleeing; no arrests were reported. State security and military personnel cordoned off the scene. Local media counted her as the 97th woman murdered in Sinaloa in 2026 and the 18th in September alone, while the state Fiscalía had opened at least 14 formal feminicidio investigation files for the month as of mid-September.

title: Day 785: Armed Group Abducts Young Man and Sets His House on Fire in Culiacán's Campo El Diez
detail: At around 10:41 PM on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, at least six armed men traveling in two pickup trucks forced their way into a home in the Piggy Back sector of Campo El Diez, southern Culiacán, at the intersection of Calle Tercera/Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla and Roberto Laviaga. The occupants beat and abducted a 20-year-old identified as Gerardo Ulises 'N' before fleeing with him to an unknown location; as they left, one attacker threw a gasoline bottle inside the house, starting a fire. Culiacán firefighters extinguished the blaze before it spread further; the victim had not been located as of the initial reports.

media.caption: Firefighters respond after an armed group abducted Gerardo Ulises and set his home ablaze in Culiacán's Campo El Diez, September 16, 2026

title: Day 785: Gunmen in Sedan Attack Scrap-Metal Shop in Culiacán's Díaz Ordaz Neighborhood
detail: Around 4:30 PM on September 16, 2026, occupants of a white sedan opened fire on a scrap-metal buying-and-selling stand at the corner of Constituyentes Ciro Ceballos and Cándido Aguilar streets in the Gustavo Díaz Ordaz neighborhood of western Culiacán, then fled. Roughly three workers were inside at the time and were unharmed; the attack caused only material damage to the storefront. SEDENA personnel secured the scene and state investigators recovered spent shell casings.

media.caption: Military personnel secure a scrap-metal shop attacked with gunfire in Culiacán's Díaz Ordaz neighborhood, September 16, 2026

title: Day 785: Arsonists Ram Gate and Burn American-Goods Store Near Culiacán's Ninth Military Zone
detail: After 1:00 AM on September 16, 2026, unidentified individuals used a vehicle to break through the entrance gate of the 'JUCLA' American-goods store at the corner of Fray Gerónimo de Mendieta street and Abelardo Medina avenue in Culiacán's Guadalupe Victoria neighborhood — a few blocks from the Novena Zona Militar army base — then set the interior on fire. Firefighters extinguished the blaze; merchandise and store fixtures suffered heavy damage. The owner announced a temporary closure of remaining branches while the Fiscalía General del Estado investigates; no arrests had been reported and no motive was confirmed.
confidenceReason: Motive and perpetrators unconfirmed; no attribution to a specific faction reported by any outlet as of publication.

title: Day 785: Man Shot Six Times Outside His Home at the Southern Exit of Villa Unión, Mazatlán
detail: At around 4:18 PM on September 16, 2026, armed men arrived at a residence at the southern exit of Villa Unión, in Mazatlán municipality, and shot a 39-year-old man identified as René, originally from Durango, six times before fleeing. Municipal police responded to reports of gunfire and requested emergency medical services; Villa Unión firefighter-paramedics gave first aid before transporting him to a hospital in serious condition.

title: Day 785: Gunmen Throw Homemade Explosive Into Vacant House in Mazatlán's Colosio Sí Neighborhood
detail: Around 5:00 PM on September 16, 2026, armed men stepped out of a vehicle on Sonora street near Francisco González Bocanegra avenue in Mazatlán's Colosio Sí neighborhood and threw a homemade explosive device through a window of a house, causing a loud blast that damaged the window and part of the facade. The house was unoccupied at the time and no injuries were reported. Municipal police, Army and Navy personnel cordoned off the area and specialized units processed the scene, confirming it was an improvised explosive device — an escalation in tactics for a wave of arson and gun attacks that has hit Mazatlán and Culiacán in recent days.
